data.name: My Personal Angel
data.detailed_description:
My Personal Angel is a black and white visual novel about the complexities of relations between people.

It often rains in our city, and sometimes it's difficult to differ the day from the night. Almost always the sky covered in dark gray clouds. Maybe because the city itself is a port, and the endless splashing of the raging sea.

Now is a difficult time. We earn money with Erica as we can: we donate blood, we collect bottles, we distribute leaflets. I work as a loader, she is a cleaner. But everything earned is spent on renting a small one-room apartment in a seedy district.

I often ask myself: "Why is this happening to me?" What did I do wrong?" But still I can't find the answer.

A few months ago a plane crashed near our city.

It is rumored that one of the passengers in the business class was a well-known sheikh, who carried a large amount of money with him. And money, especially big money, is usually kept in suitcases or safes. And often, in fires, hurricanes, explosions and so on - they remain intact. Find at least a million - you can already live on bank interest from this amount.

And I couldn't help but take a chance.

reviews.review:
This is gonna be hard, guys.
The review is mixed.
Why? Well, this visual novel has many choices, has many good points - it's entirely in black and white, which suits the depressive mood; graphics are great in my view, both characters and backgrounds, they're quite customized and I liked them a lot. And as I said it's not a kinetic visual novel, you're gonna see many different endings.
But there are some heavy negative points. Most of all the price - it costs 10$/€ which is WAY TOO MUCH for such a game. And the lack of options. It's clearly something indie-made, but really there is not a single visual novel option. You can't skip the dialogue, even the already-read one, so that going through the whole story in order to get all the endings is a long pain in the ass. You can just employ an autoclicker and rush through it all.. the only settings are related to music and sound effects (quite boring actually), so that you can't intervene by any means on the text flow.
This said, I've read on the awesome guide posted a year ago here on Steam about the save function which doesn't work (neither for me) and for a skip option that in my gameplay hasn't appeared - it should appear, following that guide, by right-clicking after the first day. I didn't manage to get it, but it may be also related to the fact that I played it on a crappy pc rather than my gaming one, being this a simple visual novel.
Anyways, it's still a downside - the game is very slow, and so are the transitions; in order to get all the endings you're still (even according to the guides) bound and forced to go through the whole story multiple times including the already-read text, which is.. a lot.
The whole plot revolves around depression and gloom, with the usual story-changing event (in this case, a plane full of money crashing near the port in which the characters are working and struggling through their lives). The story though manages to get its own strength going on - although as I was saying, playing everything tons of times is definitely annoying; especially for what concerns the fate of Anya and Erica, as you'll see progressing through the game.
It's a good story overall, if you like visual novels dealing with depressing and sad themes; it's clearly translated from Russian but it's a nice work in the end and well, it's definitely not a masterpiece (and it's not worth its price) but it's a nice title, not so easy to find among visual novels that usually treat themes like girls, love and romance with anime-like graphics.
All in all, if you find this game on discount, get it. It's a good visual novel, quite particular in its style - black and white, dealing with sadness before and after the events, with lots of characters and locations. It's surely slow and be aware that some functions like save/load or skip could or could not work for you. I overall liked it, although I didn't manage to get all the endings yet. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes these themes in visual novels, being just aware for the price and the flaws - among them, the impossibility to view the artwork apart from when you're actually playing in them.
